newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-GPT sees office better than retail.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-GPT sees office better than retail.

text.p: General Property Trust (GPT) said on Thursday it expected office property values to grow but saw the outlook for retail property as mixed.
The Lend Lease Corp managed trust said it would therefore continue to re-weight its property portfolio from retail into office property.

"Looking forward, we expect growth in capital values in most office properties over the next few years. However, changes in retail property values are expected to continue to be mixed," GPT Management chief executive David Ross said in GPT's profit statement.

"In keeping with our strategy, future changes to the major property sector weightings will more likely see an increase to office property than retail, although counter-cyclical opportunities will not be ignored," Ross said.
GPT increased the office portion of its total portfolio to 40 percent from 31 percent in 1996, while its retail portion fell to 59 percent from 67 percent.
Earlier, GPT reported a 36.7 percent rise in net profit to A$167.72 million for the year to December 31, but that was partly due to GPT's acquisition of the GEM trusts last year.
GPT's annual distribution fell to 19.9 cents per unit from 20.7 cents.
Ross said the distribution was in line with market expectations.
GPT's net tangible asset (NTA) per unit backing fell to A$2.49 from A$2.71 in 1996, due to the exercise of GPT options in June 1996 and the acquisition of the GEM trusts.
Property revaluations of Victorian retail property in particular also had a negative effect on NTA.
GPT management said it would assess industrial and other sectors of the property market and might also invest in property securities if strategic investment opportunities offered good value.
GPT's borrowings were A$375 million at the end of December, up from A$170 million a year earlier.
This had increased GPT's borrowing ratio to 11 percent from eight percent, but this was within the trust's limit of 25 percent of total assets, GPT said.
GPT's unit price was up two cents at A$2.43 at 11.00 a.m. (0000 GMT).
